"executive_summary": "This prospective single-center cohort study investigated whether chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesion length influences angiographic and clinical outcomes after successful drug-eluting stent (DES)–based percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in the DES era. A total of 235 consecutive CTO patients treated with DES between November 2004 and October 2010 at Korea University Guro Hospital were divided into a long CTO group (angiographic lesion length ≥30 mm, n=159) and a short CTO group (<30 mm, n=76). Six-month angiographic outcomes were assessed by quantitative coronary angiography, and two-year clinical outcomes were evaluated through face-to-face interviews, medical record review, and telephone contact. The primary angiographic endpoint was binary restenosis at 6–12 months, and the primary clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as the composite of total death, recurrent myocardial infarction (MI), and revascularization including PCI and coronary artery bypass graft (CABG). Baseline characteristics were similar between groups except that prior PCI was more frequent in the long CTO group and bifurcation lesions were more frequent in the short CTO group. In-hospital complications were comparable except for a higher incidence of significant intimal dissection in the long CTO group. At six months, angiographic outcomes were similar between groups, including binary restenosis (19.1% vs. 8.8%, p=0.12), in-stent restenosis (33.3% vs. 26.6%, p=0.42), and late loss (0.65 ± 0.82 mm vs. 0.46 ± 0.56 mm, p=0.13). Over two years, hard clinical endpoints were comparable: total death (3.1% vs. 5.2%, p=0.43), cardiac death (1.2% vs. 2.6%, p=0.45), MI (1.8% vs. 2.6%, p=0.71), and MACE (21.3% vs. 13.1%, p=0.13). However, repeat PCI was significantly higher in the long CTO group (18.8% vs. 7.8%, p<0.05), predominantly driven by target vessel revascularization (TVR, 16.3% vs. 6.5%, p<0.05). Multivariate analysis identified long CTO as an independent predictor of repeat PCI (OR; 4.26, CI 1.53–11.9, p=0.006). The authors conclude that, despite successful DES-based PCI, long CTO lesions are associated with a higher rate of repeat revascularization, though this did not translate into differences in mortality, cardiac death, or MACE. The study acknowledges limitations including its non-randomized, single-center, prospective registry design, small sample size, incomplete follow-up angiography, and insufficient follow-up duration. These findings suggest that while long CTO lesions carry a higher revascularization burden, the overall safety profile and long-term hard clinical outcomes remain comparable to short CTO lesions, underscoring the need for larger, longer-term studies to draw definitive conclusions.",

summary.title: Impact of Chronic Total Occlusion Lesion Length on Six-month Angiographic and 2-year Clinical Outcomes
summary.authors: Jihun Ahn; Byounggeol Choi; Yeon Choi; Jae Kyeong Byun; Ahmed Mashaly; Kareem Abdelshafi; Yoonjee Park; Young Jang; Woohyeun Kim; Eunjin Park; Jin Oh Na; Cheol Ung Choi; Eungju Kim; Chang Gyu Park; Hongseog Seo; Dongjoo Oh; Jinsu Byeon; Sangho Park; Hyeyon Yu; Seung-Woon W Rha
summary.executive_summary: This prospective single-center cohort study investigated whether chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesion length influences angiographic and clinical outcomes after successful drug-eluting stent (DES)–based percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in the DES era. A total of 235 consecutive CTO patients treated with DES between November 2004 and October 2010 at Korea University Guro Hospital were divided into a long CTO group (angiographic lesion length ≥30 mm, n=159) and a short CTO group (<30 mm, n=76). Six-month angiographic outcomes were assessed by quantitative coronary angiography, and two-year clinical outcomes were evaluated through face-to-face interviews, medical record review, and telephone contact. The primary angiographic endpoint was binary restenosis at 6–12 months, and the primary clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as the composite of total death, recurrent myocardial infarction (MI), and revascularization including PCI and coronary artery bypass graft (CABG). Baseline characteristics were similar between groups except that prior PCI was more frequent in the long CTO group and bifurcation lesions were more frequent in the short CTO group. In-hospital complications were comparable except for a higher incidence of significant intimal dissection in the long CTO group. At six months, angiographic outcomes were similar between groups, including binary restenosis (19.1% vs. 8.8%, p=0.12), in-stent restenosis (33.3% vs. 26.6%, p=0.42), and late loss (0.65 ± 0.82 mm vs. 0.46 ± 0.56 mm, p=0.13). Over two years, hard clinical endpoints were comparable: total death (3.1% vs. 5.2%, p=0.43), cardiac death (1.2% vs. 2.6%, p=0.45), MI (1.8% vs. 2.6%, p=0.71), and MACE (21.3% vs. 13.1%, p=0.13). However, repeat PCI was significantly higher in the long CTO group (18.8% vs. 7.8%, p<0.05), predominantly driven by target vessel revascularization (TVR, 16.3% vs. 6.5%, p<0.05). Multivariate analysis identified long CTO as an independent predictor of repeat PCI (OR; 4.26, CI 1.53–11.9, p=0.006). The authors conclude that, despite successful DES-based PCI, long CTO lesions are associated with a higher rate of repeat revascularization, though this did not translate into differences in mortality, cardiac death, or MACE. The study acknowledges limitations including its non-randomized, single-center, prospective registry design, small sample size, incomplete follow-up angiography, and insufficient follow-up duration. These findings suggest that while long CTO lesions carry a higher revascularization burden, the overall safety profile and long-term hard clinical outcomes remain comparable to short CTO lesions, underscoring the need for larger, longer-term studies to draw definitive conclusions.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This prospective single-center cohort study investigated whether chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesion length influences angiographic and clinical outcomes after successful drug-eluting stent (DES)–based percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in the DES era. A total of 235 consecutive CTO patients treated with DES between November 2004 and October 2010 at Korea University Guro Hospital were divided into a long CTO group (angiographic lesion length ≥30 mm, n=159) and a short CTO group (<30 mm, n=76). Six-month angiographic outcomes were assessed by quantitative coronary angiography, and two-year clinical outcomes were evaluated through face-to-face interviews, medical record review, and telephone contact. The primary angiographic endpoint was binary restenosis at 6–12 months, and the primary clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as the composite of total death, recurrent myocardial infarction (MI), and revascularization including PCI and coronary artery bypass graft (CABG). Baseline characteristics were similar between groups except that prior PCI was more frequent in the long CTO group and bifurcation lesions were more frequent in the short CTO group. In-hospital complications were comparable except for a higher incidence of significant intimal dissection in the long CTO group. At six months, angiographic outcomes were similar between groups, including binary restenosis (19.1% vs. 8.8%, p=0.12), in-stent restenosis (33.3% vs. 26.6%, p=0.42), and late loss (0.65 ± 0.82 mm vs. 0.46 ± 0.56 mm, p=0.13). Over two years, hard clinical endpoints were comparable: total death (3.1% vs. 5.2%, p=0.43), cardiac death (1.2% vs. 2.6%, p=0.45), MI (1.8% vs. 2.6%, p=0.71), and MACE (21.3% vs. 13.1%, p=0.13). However, repeat PCI was significantly higher in the long CTO group (18.8% vs. 7.8%, p<0.05), predominantly driven by target vessel revascularization (TVR, 16.3% vs. 6.5%, p<0.05). Multivariate analysis identified long CTO as an independent predictor of repeat PCI (OR; 4.26, CI 1.53–11.9, p=0.006). The authors conclude that, despite successful DES-based PCI, long CTO lesions are associated with a higher rate of repeat revascularization, though this did not translate into differences in mortality, cardiac death, or MACE. The study acknowledges limitations including its non-randomized, single-center, prospective registry design, small sample size, incomplete follow-up angiography, and insufficient follow-up duration. These findings suggest that while long CTO lesions carry a higher revascularization burden, the overall safety profile and long-term hard clinical outcomes remain comparable to short CTO lesions, underscoring the need for larger, longer-term studies to draw definitive conclusions.

Research Context
CTO PCI outcomes depend on baseline lesion characteristics and clinical risk factors. Long coronary artery lesions are a worse prognostic factor after PCI. CTO procedural success remains lower than non-CTO despite device advances. Lesion length predicts MACE and restenosis in non-CTO DES treatment. CTO clinical and angiographic outcomes remain worse than non-CTO disease. No definitive answers exist regarding CTO outcomes by lesion length in the DES era.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central research question concerns the impact of CTO lesion length on outcomes. The study hypothesized that adverse outcomes would be more frequent in long CTO lesions. Long CTO lesions carry worse clinical risk factors such as prior MI and PCI. Newer generation DES use was more common in the short CTO group. The predicted outcome was higher repeat PCI and TVR in long CTO lesions. The predicted outcome was worse angiographic outcomes at six months.

Methodological Details
The study enrolled 235 consecutive CTO patients treated with DES. Patients were treated between November 2004 and October 2010. The study was conducted at Korea University Guro Hospital in Seoul. Patients were divided into long and short CTO groups by lesion length. The long CTO group included 159 patients with lesion length ≥30mm. The short CTO group included 76 patients with lesion length <30mm. The study protocol was approved by the institutional review board. All patients provided informed consent to participate. CTO was defined by TIMI flow grade 0 and duration ≥3 months. Only de novo lesions were included; in-stent restenosis was excluded. Loading doses of clopidogrel and aspirin were administered pre-procedure. Maintenance dual antiplatelet therapy included aspirin and clopidogrel. Clopidogrel was encouraged to continue for at least one year. Cilostazol use depended on physician discretion. PCI procedures followed current guidelines using standard techniques. Atheroablative devices were not utilized in the procedures. Simple balloon pre-dilation was mostly performed. All PCI was performed using drug-eluting stents. DES type was decided by the operator during procedures. Procedural success required diameter stenosis <30% and TIMI grade ≥2. QCA parameters were measured before, after, and at 6 months. The primary angiographic endpoint was binary restenosis at 6-12 months. Secondary angiographic endpoints included ISR, DS, MLD, and LL. Two-year follow-up used interviews, records, and telephone contact. The primary clinical endpoint was MACE. MACE included total death, recurrent MI, and revascularization. Deaths were considered cardiac unless non-cardiac death was confirmed. Continuous variables were analyzed with Student's t-test. Categorical variables were analyzed with χ2 or Fisher's exact test. Logistic regression adjusted for multiple risk factors. A p-value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant. All analyses were performed using SPSS 20.

Procedures And Architectures
QCA measurement was performed at the study hospital. Follow-up angiography was obtained in 99 of 159 long CTO patients. Follow-up angiography was obtained in 45 of 76 short CTO patients. The logistic regression model estimated risk of repeat PCI and TVR. Long CTO was an independent predictor for repeat PCI. Long CTO was an independent predictor for TVR. The study used Table 1 for baseline characteristics. The study used Table 2 for complications. The study used Table 3 for clinical outcomes. The study used Table 4 for predictors. The study used Table 5 for angiographic outcomes. Six-month angiographic outcomes were presented in Table 5. The long CTO group had 99 patients in angiographic follow-up. The short CTO group had 45 patients in angiographic follow-up.

Key Results
Baseline characteristics were similar except prior PCI frequency. Bifurcation lesions were more frequent in the short CTO group. In-hospital complications were similar except intimal dissection. Total death was 3.1% vs. 5.2% between groups. Cardiac death was 1.2% vs. 2.6% between groups. MI was 1.8% vs. 2.6% between groups. MACE was 21.3% vs. 13.1% between groups. Repeat PCI was 18.8% vs. 7.8% in the long CTO group. TVR was 16.3% vs. 6.5% in the long CTO group. The incidence of repeat PCI was higher in the long CTO group. Long CTO was an important predictor for repeat PCI. The odds ratio for repeat PCI was 4.26 with CI 1.53-11.9. Angiographic follow-up was obtained in 62% of long CTO patients. Angiographic follow-up was obtained in 59% of short CTO patients. The incidence of ISR was 33.3% vs. 26.6% between groups. Binary restenosis was 19.1% vs. 8.8% between groups. Late loss was 0.65 ± 0.82 mm vs. 0.46 ± 0.56 mm. The incidence of binary restenosis was higher in the long CTO group. Vessel diameter was 3.11 ± 0.43 mm vs. 2.92 ± 0.42 mm. The odds ratio for TVR was 4.23 with CI 1.52-11.8. The higher TVR incidence did not translate into hard endpoints. The safety profile was similar between the two groups. The mid-term angiographic outcomes were similar between groups. The higher repeat PCI incidence was despite DES implantation.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Long CTO lesions carry a higher revascularization burden. The higher TVR did not translate into critical hard endpoints. This pattern was reported previously from the j-Cypher Registry. Less myocardial viability may lessen the harmful effect of restenosis. Collateral channels may lessen the harmful effect of restenosis. These factors could lessen the physiologic effect of restenosis. The binary restenosis trend may increase over time. The higher repeat PCI supports this hypothesis. The vessel diameter difference did not affect outcomes significantly. The study investigated a real-world CTO cohort prospectively. Long-term studies with larger numbers are required. Larger study populations are necessary for final conclusions.

Contradictions And Limitations
The study was not a randomized controlled trial. The study was a single center registry. Baseline characteristics were slightly different between groups. Newer generation DES use differed between groups. Unmeasured confounders and analytical bias could exist. Follow-up angiography was not routinely performed. Follow-up angiography depended on ischemic symptoms. Collaterals and viability could influence ischemic symptoms. The sample size was relatively small. The study lacked power to prove angiographic differences. The two-year follow-up was not long enough. The binary restenosis trend may increase over time. The higher repeat PCI supports the hypothesis.

Long CTO lesions are associated with higher repeat PCI and TVR after successful DES-based PCI. The incidence of repeat PCI was higher in the long CTO group. Late loss was 0.65 ± 0.82 mm vs. 0.46 ± 0.56 mm. The long and short CTO groups showed similar angiographic outcomes. The angiographic outcomes were similar between groups. Robustness And Ablation Notes
The study was not a randomized controlled trial. The study was a single center registry. Baseline characteristics were slightly different between groups. Unmeasured confounders and analytical bias could exist. Follow-up angiography was not routinely performed. The sample size was relatively small. The study lacked power to prove angiographic differences. The two-year follow-up was not long enough. The binary restenosis trend may increase over time. The higher repeat PCI supports this hypothesis.

Ethical Considerations
The study protocol was approved by the institutional review board. All patients provided informed consent to participate. The study was conducted at Korea University Guro Hospital. No ethical concerns were raised beyond standard consent.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is that long CTO lesions carry a higher revascularization burden. 2. The strongest evidence is the multivariate odds ratio for repeat PCI. 3. The future path is long-term studies with larger study populations.
